name: com.linsays/lin-says
title: Lin Says: spoken English practice
description: Say it naturally in English, phrase explanations, role-plays and pronunciation-check links.

tools.name: how_to_say_in_english
tools.description: Turn what someone wants to say (in any language, or their own rough English) into natural spoken English: three ways to say it (casual, neutral, polite), the word-for-word version to avoid and why, and a short example conversation. Use when a learner asks how to say something in English or whether their sentence sounds natural.

text.description: What the person wants to say, in any language (up to 100 characters).

language.description: Language for explanations and translations: en, zh (Simplified Chinese), zh-Hant, es, pt, vi, ja or id. Default en. The English to say is always in English.

tools.name: explain_english_phrase
tools.description: Explain an English word, phrase or sentence for a learner: what it means (in the learner's language when given), when to use it, a short example, IPA for a single word, and for a word with Latin or Greek parts, those parts as its Wiktionary etymology shows them. Use when a learner asks what something means, e.g. "fair point meaning" or "walk me through 什么意思".

phrase.description: The English word, phrase or sentence (up to 120 characters).

language.description: Language for explanations and translations: en, zh (Simplified Chinese), zh-Hant, es, pt, vi, ja or id. Default en. The English to say is always in English.

tools.name: find_english_conversation_scenes
tools.description: Search Lin Says' library of about 400 real-life spoken-English situations (ordering coffee, returning an item, a job interview, seeing a doctor…) by meaning, in any language. Returns matching scenes with links; each scene has a short animated video, the full script at three levels, shadowing with word-by-word pronunciation feedback and AI role-play. Returns nothing when no scene fits: then use write_roleplay_scene.

query.description: The situation, in any language (2 to 80 characters), e.g. "return a jacket", "看牙医".

tools.name: write_roleplay_scene
tools.description: Write a short spoken-English conversation (8 to 10 lines, checked by a second pass) for any situation the learner describes, at their level, with key phrases; returns the script and a link where they can shadow each line with pronunciation feedback and act it out with an AI partner. Takes 10 to 20 seconds.

situation.description: The situation to practise, in any language (up to 200 characters), e.g. "asking my landlord to fix the heating".

language.description: Language for explanations and translations: en, zh (Simplified Chinese), zh-Hant, es, pt, vi, ja or id. Default en. The English to say is always in English.

tools.name: pronunciation_practice_link
tools.description: Get a link that opens Lin Says' pronunciation lab with an English sentence filled in: the learner says it out loud and sees which words came out wrong, what they sounded like and how to fix them. Use after giving someone an English sentence to say; an assistant cannot hear the learner, this page can.

sentence.description: The English sentence to practise (up to 300 characters).
